file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance equipped with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
I’ll give you two ways to do it:

1. **`gcloud` CLI** – the easiest way if you already have the Cloud SDK installed.  
2. **REST API** – the raw HTTP request you could send from any HTTP client (curl, Postman, your own script, etc.).

> ⚠️ **Prerequisites**  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project (`PROJECT_ID`) with billing enabled.  
> * The **Compute Engine API** must be enabled for that project.  
> * You need the **Compute Engine Admin** role (or equivalent) on the project.  
> * If you’re using the REST API, you’ll need an OAuth 2.0 access token with the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`.  

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Set your project and zone first
export PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
export ZONE="us-central1-a"

# Create a VM named "rtx-a6000-demo" with:
#   • n1-standard-8 (8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM)
#   • 1 NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU
#   • Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (focal)
#   • 100 GB SSD boot disk
#   • Preemptible (optional – remove if you don’t want it)
#   • Allow SSH via the default network
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-demo \
    --project=${PROJECT_ID} \
    --zone=${ZONE} \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
    --preemptible \
    --tags=http-server,https-server \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh # optional: add a startup script
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds GPUs. Format: `type=<GPU_TYPE>,count=<NUM>` |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Selects the OS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | Disk size/type. |
| `--preemptible` | Makes the instance preemptible (cheaper, but can be terminated after 24h). Remove if you want a regular instance. |
| `--tags` | Network tags for firewall rules. |

> **Tip:** If you want a *regular* (non‑preemptible) instance, simply drop the `--preemptible` flag.

---

## 2. Using the REST API

Below is a **JSON payload** you would POST to the Compute Engine Instances endpoint.  
Replace placeholders (`{PROJECT_ID}`, `{ZONE}`) with your actual values.

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-demo",
  "machineType": "zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "labels": {
    "env": "demo"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y python3-pip"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

### Making the HTTP request

```bash
# Assuming you have an OAuth 2.0 access token in $ACCESS_TOKEN
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/zones/${ZONE}/instances?alt=json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

Where `instance.json` contains the JSON payload above.

> **Note:**  
> * The `acceleratorType` field uses the full resource path.  
> * If you want a **preemptible** instance, add `"preemptible": true` under the top-level object.  
> * The `metadata` section can include a `startup-script` that runs automatically when the instance boots.

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Project ID & Zone set |
| ✅ | Compute Engine API enabled |
| ✅ | Proper IAM permissions |
| ✅ | GPU quota available for `nvidia-tesla-a6000` |
| ✅ | Billing enabled |
| ✅ | (Optional) Firewall rules allow SSH/HTTP/HTTPS |

If you hit any quota limits, you can request an increase from the **Quotas** page in the Cloud Console.

Happy computing! 🚀
